zh: 一个前端如果连最小的未配对后端都赢不了，就赢不了任何后端，可以直接放弃；如果能赢，让它去配最小的后端最不浪费。
两组都升序排序，用指针j指向最小的未配对后端；按从小到大遍历前端，若当前前端严格大于b[j]，就配成一对并让j前进，否则跳过这个前端。
排序a和b，j=0；对a中的每个值v：若j小于n且v严格大于b[j]，则j加1。遍历结束后j就是最大配对数。注意相等不算胜过。
en: A frontend that cannot beat the smallest unmatched backend cannot beat any backend, so drop it; one that can should take the smallest backend, which wastes nothing.

Sort both groups ascending and let j point at the smallest unmatched backend; go through the frontends from small to large, and when the current frontend is strictly greater than b[j], pair them and advance j; otherwise skip that frontend.
Sort a and b, j = 0; for each v in a, if j < n and v > b[j], increase j. When the loop ends, j is the maximum number of pairs. Equal values do not count as a win.

explanationEn:
## Approach

Sort both lists and pair each backend with the smallest unused frontend that can beat it.

## Proof of correctness

If the smallest frontend is not large enough, it cannot beat any larger backend either, so it can be skipped; if it can be paired, some optimal plan can be changed by exchanging pairings so that these two smallest available elements form a pair, without reducing the count. Repeating the exchange proves the greedy optimal.

## Complexity

Time O(n log n), space O(n).
